grades.quote: FLT.S and FLE.S perform what the IEEE 754-2008 standard refers to as _signaling_ comparisons: that is, they set the invalid operation exception flag if either input is NaN. FEQ.S performs a _quiet_ comparison: it only sets the invalid operation exception flag if either input is a signaling NaN. For all three instructions, the result is 0 if either operand is NaN.
grades.reason: Directly explains RISC-V F-extension FEQ.S/FLT.S/FLE.S behavior with NaN operands: result is 0, and which instructions raise the invalid flag for any NaN (FLT/FLE, signaling) versus only signaling NaN (FEQ, quiet).
Only an encoding table for RV32D instructions including FEQ.D/FLT.D/FLE.D; says nothing about NaN handling or exception flags.
